Maintenance Report — MNT-0011-009

Asset: WELL-0011 (SW-23 Well 011, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: downhole pump Work started: 12 May 2024 08:00 · Finished: 28 May 2024 16:00 · Well stopped for this job: 392 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Daniel Foster, Kevin Price Triggered by: inspection INS-0011-0080 on 2024-05-09 Report written: 28 May 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that fluid stopped reaching the flowline and the rod load spiked on the downstroke. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0011-0080 showed the wellhead at 27.7 °C with the air at 25.9 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale. The company workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 14 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

A worn plunger that let sand settle and lock the pump.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 5 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rods and the insert pump.
  3. Inspected the pump: sand in the barrel and a worn plunger.
  4. Ran in a new insert pump.
  5. Re-spaced the pump and hung the rods back on.

Summary of the fix: pulled and replaced downhole pump.

Testing and return to service

Pump test confirmed fluid to surface and the wellhead warmed back to normal. The well was returned to production.
